i was really quite surpsrised by climbey. the graphics and art style leave a lot to be desired, but the rest of the game blew my expectations away.

climbey is a fun, simple game with potentially infinite content. this is the exact type of game i want to see on vr. easy to pick up yet is challenging, has responsive controls, and tons of non-repetitive content. it doesn't require a lot of room to play either, despite how much movement is in the game. most of your real life movement will be arm flailing. your character is far from stagnant, however. the walking mechanic has restored my faith that future vr titles can do locomotion well. it works well and feels natural. jumping works just fine as well, but it's tricky to be accurate with it, and is one of the hardest parts of the game. i'm not sure if i have just gotten more use to vr or if it's the natural movements you have to make with your body to walk and jump in this game, but i did not feel any m otion sickness.

the user created levels expand the potential content of this game to the moon.  it's fun sitting in a lobby with other players and listent to the chit chat as every tries to make it through a course someone created.

the game is a bit physically demanding. not to a great degree, but enough to break you out in a sweat. just know what you're getting into. this is not a relax and unwind kind of game.

i think climbey is a must-have for new vr owners. don't pass it up because it looks lackluster like i did initially. looks can be deceiving.

last july, i went to the first stop of the htc vive live truck tour in san diego. i expected to try out a virtual reality headset and either be unimpressed or think it was kind of cool. then they loaded up tilt brush as my second demo and i could paint and actually see depth as i painted in three dimensions. this was a huge deal to me as i can't see 3d in movies or in those magic frame pictures that require you to be able to see 3d to appreciate.

i drew some flowers that day and signed a letter e for the first initial of my name.

six months later i got to draw a purple monster that started out as a hut and ended up looking like a pac-man ghost in front of skillman and hackett at the steam vr developer showcase. it was a pivotal moment in my life where i could thank the creators personally for one of the most remarkable art applications available on the market.

despite the sappy emotional story, i encourage everyone at any age to pick up the vive controllers and create something in tilt brush. i can't wait to see what fellow vive owners and their friends come up with now that it is commercially available!

review_feedback: Hi there! Firstly we want to convey our sincerest apologies for how late our response is to your feedback. We appreciate looking back we should've actioned our early post launch reviews a lot sooner. We're sorry we didn't and we hope you can forgive us for that. Secondly your incredibly positive review is massively appreciated! :) It's very humbling to compare us to some of the visuals which can be experienced on a PCVR game. :) We're not sure if you're aware but we do also have a steam and rift version of the game so if you have a gaming PC or laptop you can play our PC version of the game. We're also cross buy enabled on oculus so you'll get the rift version for free. :) We certainly spent a long time developing the game across all platforms and we aimed to have everything ready on those platforms for the same date. Obviously with the quest there were some sacrifices we made but at the time we got it as close as we could with what we hard to work with. :) Not sure if you've followed our progress with Espire by the way but we've also spent the last 18 months or so improving the game where possible. The visuals you loved in the game post launch have now been significantly improved further so you'll see things like reflections and roughness on certain surfaces, more solid looking textures, better meshing etc. We also improved on the enemy AI detection and stability so guards will react more realistically and detect you in areas you would expect and won't detect you in areas you wouldn't expect them to catch you. :) Game performance is also a lot smoother and loading times have been heavily reduced. :) We also found time to incorporate additional content into the game in the form of new challenges. These bring new category types such as intel and weapons which can provide some unique gameplay as well as a couple of new weapons and new maps. :) We do hope you'll check the game out again if it's been a while as we trust you'll love the improved present version of the game. :) Thanks again for all the amazing support and again very sorry for our late response. :)

rapidly becoming my second job.

 might as well get the s.t.a.l.k.e.r. comparisons out of the way now:  it's not 1:1 but man the vibe is there.  there aren't any npcs like duty or freedom, but after that it's mostly all here.  throw something at an anomaly so you can avoid it.  get snuck up on by a low opacity monster.  pick up a magic jewel from the middle floating train wreck.  use a console command (conveniently placed right in the pause menu) to unstick yourself from some geometry.  a lot of care has been put in to really give an authentic feel that this is what it'd be like if massive radiation spills were magical.  i have traversed areas suspended in time and warped in space, inimical to life and alien to human minds.  

the game borders on simulation.  it's more than just the part where you have to clean your own guns.  in combat, if your magazines run empty, it'll be some time before you can put bullets back in them, and if bullets are not boxed, you will be reloading by hand.  i do not recommend going into the zone without a complete weapons check and maybe a couple spare mags in your backpack... which you access by pulling it around off your back, and storing in a 3-d pack.  items can overlap in this "hammerspace" and if you don't keep your bag organized, you will at best be frustrated, and in an emergency, probably killed.  going out in the dark is extremely ill-advised and i've had to crash out in an empty grain silo to wait out the night.  i sit on the mattress, crack open a can of moose meat, and play a cassette i found next to a dead scientist.  when i clean my guns, i light a cigarette first.  i have to clean my room.  it's full of loose ammo and half full ammo boxes.  i am dangerously close to listening to hard base and wearing adidas during play.  i don't own adidas, and i worry that i would not hear police mimics over the cyka blyat.  

this is as close to enjoying camping as i've ever been.

i am always wanting to go back.  i look forward to it. i think about it while at work.  it is impinging on social time.  the atmosphere and exploration approach super metroid.

[u]this is a neutral recommendation.[/u] i'll be honest, i didn't really enjoy playing this game, but i do think there's enough here that i can at least give it a neutral recommendation, which doesn't exist on steam. i would definitely give it a sideways thumb if possible. i think the game has merit, if nothing else, for its unique gameplay for vr. 

i would describe this game as a mix of auto-battler, action rpg hack n slash, card summoner, and rogue-lite. it has an interesting premise and a promising gameplay loop that can be improved upon and refined. however, currently, as is, it's just too simple and the jankiness / bugs bring the experience down. i didn't have fun, but i could see others who are into auto-battlers maybe enjoying this, even if it's pretty basic. the game seemed to be mostly about making one strong card and spamming that ability. are you doing enough damage is the strategy. if not, try again after upgrading some more.

game is running on the unity engine. on my rtx 3080, i was getting a steady 72fps (default on q3). i did experience some bugs, the biggest one being that i would get stuck in the terrain. you do have full locomotion & smooth turning available. you can play seated or standing. 

needs fine-tuning on the gameplay loop before i could recommend, plus more polish overall. auto-battlers are fun because they are like a spinning plate challenge. you have to keep them all spinning or the whole thing falls apart. there's really only one plate in this game that you need to worry about and that's why it fails.

[b]rate 5/10.[/b]

review_feedback: Thanks so much for reconsidering your review. You've shared some valuable info in this post, and I think I can help get things working well for you. First, though, please absolutely make sure the boundaries you've drawn only include areas you're willing to move and punch within and that you don't have them right up against the edge of a wall or other obstacle. It doesn't have to be a huge gap, but you do want to leave a little margin of error in case the Quest didn't put the boundary exactly where you thought you drew it. If you're in roomscale mode and your boundaries are clear, you should be all set as far as the opponent staying within your free space. The game itself is actually designed around 2m by 1.5m of space as a minimum (up to 4m by 4m maximum), but I list 2m by 2m on the Quest because that's what Oculus lists as their minimum roomscale size on Quest. The way the Quest picks its "forward" direction is a little mysterious to me, but I have a couple of ways in the game that you can change it. First, if you want to pick a completely new forward direction for the game to use, hold down the menu button for a couple of seconds - i.e., the button that's like the normal recenter button, but on the other controller. I use that one because the Quest handles recenter requests itself instead of passing the request on to the game, and it doesn't do anything for games that are in roomscale mode (the Rift lets the game handle the recenter request even when in roomscale mode, and that version of TotF uses the normal recenter button to pick a new forward direction, as you'd expect). Doing this will take whatever edge of your play area (the red rectangle on the floor) that you're looking at and make it the new "front" side. The next thing you can do is go into the in-game Settings menu and change the "In-Match Turn Direction" setting. That makes your forward direction different when you're in a match compared to when you're not in one. You can use that to, for example, make the menu screen be 3m side-to-side while having the matches be 3m front-to-back, which is probably what I'd recommend for the shape of the play area you have. Please feel free to email me at fyiandev@gmail.com, and I'll be happy to help if you have any questions about getting these configured. Thanks!

i'm into non-plane flight simulators, mostly birds, so a dragon sim appealed to me (and hey, it was cheap).

this game is a bit of a mess, but a fun mess.  you can fly as a dragon or a dragon rider (two available pov) around fairly small worlds, finding stuff (easter egg hunt) and taking little flight challenges like destroying balloons or making it through a long series of floating hoops.

i find the controls a bit counter-intuitive (prefer flying games where you use your arms to flap, rather than just moving joysticks) but after 15 min or so you can get used to them.  the animated dragons are actually not bad, with some nice surface detailing on the saddle, wings, etc.  the landscape is fantastical of course, and the flight physics are arcade-level;  but it has a kind of wacky charm that draws me back for casual play.

the controls are a bit complex for really young players, but for age range 10-up it is good colourful fun.  some violence appears to be possible (there are attack commands) but so far, playing casually i have had no antagonistic experiences.  the dragons can swim underwater as well as fly, which adds a bit more variety to the experience.  so what we have here is kind of like an airplane sim (control a flying craft using joysticks and buttons) with the graphics and feel of a bird sim (flapping wings, gliding and diving, hovering etc).

some kids are really, really into dragons :-)  and for these kids, this game would be a perfect match.  but even if you just like arcade level flying, it offers colourful fun.  don't expect any story line, deep engagement, or serious puzzle solving and you won't be disappointed.  it's a nice vr showcase app because of the scenery and flight options (all the way from passive tourism for newbies, to full control and aerobatic flight for the more advanced vr user).

i was excited to get into this one because of the good reviews, but holy cow, i don't understand why it has a very positive rating at all. almost everything about it... the movement, the combat, the graphics, the animation... everything, really, is bad.

let me start with the controls. it has a simple teleport and rotate locomotion, with teleport bound to left stick and rotate bound to right. except, it isn't really rotate, it's kind of a flicky-jumpy snap rotate, where you point the thumbstick in a direction, then when you release it, you'll face that direction. it doesn't work very well, it's hard to get facing exactly where you want it to, it seems to sensitive and needs to have some kind of deadzone. robo-recall is an example of this type of  movement done well. of course, if you can rotate freely in your play area, this really isn't an issue at all. the teleport itself works fine enough, but there's no kind of cooldown or restriction on it, so when you're in an enemy area, you can just whiz past everything and ignore it if no combat is required.

another thing, every action, including open inventory, pick up item, pick up weapon, sheath weapon and fire weapon, are all bound to the same trigger. the secondary, middle-finger trigger (you know, the one usually used to grasp things in vr games?) is entirely un-used. i don't really understand this... it simplifies things a bit, but when i shoot myself in the foot with a crossbow bolt when i'm trying to draw my sword, it gives me the impression things could be a bit more intuitive.

the colors in the couple landscapes i saw were a generic, deserty dull brown. neither the textures or models were of considerable quality. pretty excusable for a free vr game, to be honest. but the animatons are noticeably terrible. everything moves very unnaturally and stiffly, not convincingly humanoid at all, but the worst part is the transitions. literally every creature has no transition animations or frames. stuff will be sitting at a campfire in an awkward idle cycle, then when you get close enough for it to aggro, it'll pop up onto it's feet and start moving towards you immediately. it doesn't stand up slowly, or even quickly jump up - it's literally one frame it's sitting, and the next it's angrily charging at you. it looks like a cash-grab 3d action phone game or one of the unity asset flips people sell for five bucks on steam.

now the combat... man, it's pretty weak. visions of twilight princess on the wii come to mind, and even then i'd say that game does it better. the hit detection and implementation of the shield seem awful for a game focused mostly on sword and board combat. stuff would hit me when i actively moved my shield in the way of the attack, and passing your sword through something doesn't guarantee a hit, even if you were moving the sword fast enough. at the same time, sometimes i would accidentally make hits when i was just transitioning to another weapon or rotating to block an attack. wiggling your weapon hand in front of you seems to be the best strategy, as i managed to clear the entire first enemy area by aggroing everything with my wicked fast teleport skills, then huddling in corner with my shield raised, and waggling my sword back and forth at the wrist like i was shaking up a spray can. 

i mean, give it a try, apparently there's a lot of content, and it's free, so there's really no risk... but i had a hard time squeezing any enjoyment out of this. i am genuinely confused at the people giving this glowing reviews, it makes me feel like there's something i missed or that isn't working for me. the people saying "hit detection is bad, but the rest is really good!" are liars or dumb, because the rest of this game isn't good either.

its not meant to be half life 3 because its not meant to be played without vr.  you can with the mod - and i get big fans of the ip who cant afford the hardware want to - but they wont actually get the game they think they are getting.  

the experience, gameplay, length, content, emotions, sense of wonder etc between those two mediums are apples and oranges.  and this game was made specifically for citrus lovers.  if you are walking down a tunnel on a pc game it may take you 10 seconds with very little emotion.  just getting to that next fight, barely taking in the visuals.  but if you are inside the game, and you are actually walking down that creepy tunnel...light on ammo...unsure what is going to jump out at you and cause you to fall over your desk chair or slam your hand against a wall...that first time is a lot more than 10 seconds and you love and appreciate every second of it.

truly the first near-perfect vr game of its time.  (best played with the corresponding valve controllers but probably a minor inconvenience otherwise).  not meant to be 40+ hours - it's vr.  not meant to be constant action and unlimited ammo - there are other great vr games for that stuff.  only meant to be a promise of everything this branch of gaming could be if developers were willing to take the risks.  

hopefully it is just the beginning...not just for valve but for the industry...though 2 years later and there is still little at this level to compare.  

so don't buy it if you want to just play a normal pc mod. watch a youtube run through or summary instead and save up for the head gear. but if you have vr and haven't given it a go...you are missing something magical.

after about 10 minutes of playing this game, i really wanted to request a refund. however, i figured i should at least play 20 minutes more before i do any kind of review. well, i am glad that i did not request a refund because although this is not a great game by any stretch of the imagination, it actually has some very epic moments.

i'm rating the game a sale price rating of 6/10. so i'm not saying it's a really good game. what i am saying, is that this game is definitely a good deal for $5. you're getting quite a bit of content here. so the negative reviews mention walking around and just hacking away at enemies. 

however, there's more to the game than that. in fact, you can teleport or move in 3rd person full locomotion. i suggest you move in 3rd person full locomotion at all times and forget teleportation. teleportation is very bad in this game and i imagine it's a reason for a lot of the negative reviews. take off the option for the boundary guard as well. yes, this game automatically adds another space guard for your vr space. why? i have no idea.

once you get used to the 3rd person full locomotion, you see that moving in this game is actually pretty fast. it's not sluggish at all. you'll be quickly moving from location to location. and soon you'll discover a secret which lets you magically auto teleport to witch area locations. 

the inventory system is also weird. you press y on your oculus controller and you'll see everything you have floating in your space. then you click to read its description and consume or use it. there are lots of items in this game and soon your inventory will be an unwieldly mess. i suggest just eating as much as possible. try different weapons. i prefer double swords myself. or double mace weapons.

the main criticism is that you just hack and slash in this game. there's some truth to that, at least superficially. there is actually a stamina system in this game to prevent you from wildly swinging away. of course, you are op. you'll be taking down several enemies in no time once you figure out what the game wants you to do. basically, the trick is to block when you can and yes you can shield bash and then swing at the openings you see. i found that a bottom up and diagonal approach usually worked. but as long as you see an opening, swing away. 

there's also different types of enemies. all sorts of humans with different weapons. goblins. spiders. this tall father type dude and his midget son, i believe? they were awesome to cut down. and the map is pretty big. i spent 45 minutes in the game and not anywhere close to finishing the first quest. 

rate 6/10. 

p.s. use your weapon to break vases, chests, barrels, etc ... there's loot everywhere! oh and check out the cemeteries!

i only have 2 hours of game play at the time i type this so my review could change later. as of now, i have enjoyed the game despite quests becoming all fetch quests. i have an issue with quests not updating, however reading other reviews it seems you need to have the quest on "active" in order to count credit for it. it is a little rough that you do have to be in a specified area for some objectives but it does not ruin the game for me. i find the combat somewhat easy to handle but sometimes my melee hits do not seem to cause damage despite swinging the weapon rather aggressively. i am glad that weapons do not always one shot an enemy. it makes games too easy and boring when you always feel like a god. to me, the game plays more into a realistic combat of not everything drops in one hit. 

graphics and sound
i read a lot of people complain about the graphics and knowing this is not a "aaa" title, i am not bothered by it. sure there are things that stand out, but in the end it does not ruin the game play for me. as far as  sound goes, i have killed a few zs while they were running towards me and after they fell the sound animation was still going strong. i thought i was being attacked by another z but nothing was around. not game breaking but keeps me on my toes a lot more often. i usually turn music off or way down so i can not really say anything about the music in the game.

option selections

as of today i would recommend this game if someone asks me about playing it. i will play solo for a little while longer then eventually try out the multiplayer mode. i am hoping to keep this positive review but time will tell down the road.

exceptionally poor out of box experience, do not expect to play this game comfortably from a fresh install.

index controllers have extremely poor default steamvr bindings. you cannot play the game properly until you've messed around in steamvr's input binder first. on top of that, there is no in-game setting to configure hmd/controller relative movement, you can only do this using an .ini setting that must be configured outside the game using a text editor.

this version also neither includes nor supports fallout 4's dlcs. you will need to own the base game and manually copy the dlc files from it if you wish to play them. however, both the automatron and nuka world dlcs have major issues that needs to be addressed manually using mods, or else you will run into crashes and softlocks.

"i have my vr legs and this makes me sick!:"  ya big baby! no kidding, this ones true but exaggerated. any large, fast moving, open world ported game makes me slightly ill and this one is no different (elder scrolls, fallout, the forest, etc) thats the reality of open world ports, the game wasnt made for vr, deal with it. play for 1-2 hours and take a break.

5. "blah blah scope blah:" yeah, the scope system is lazy. it just pops up a mini tv above the gun that is zoomed in. lazy, but it works perfectly fine.

(i with it was just a button trigger).

7. "50 bucks for this?:"  fair point. i was offended at the price too, but i figure if no one pays for these companies to dip their toes into vr then they are less likely to make more vr stuff and i really want vr to be a full fledge industry instead of mini games/ tech demos that is the majority of the games now. so, ill bend over and pay my dues.

this is one of my favorite combate vr games i've ever played. there really isn't any point in combate where it feels like it's getting old, weather its impealing a wraith/ghost monster, or slicing a game. when you start the game, you only get some basic weapons, but as you progress you get your hands on better and better weapons. i won't lie, some of the swords you get at the start do feel similar without many noticable differnces, but once you are past that, it won't even matter. becuase other than those few swords at the start, all of the melee weapons feel destinct, including the normal, non-magical ones. and when you throw in the magic weapons into the pool of items you can play with, then you can truely see why this game shines with it's weapon variety. you get wands that shoot ice swords (which you can then pick up and use), shotguns which can blast through most enemies & make them drop their armor and weapons where they stood loony toons style, swords that have guns attached to them which let you stab and then blast away enemies, and soo so much more. i also like the way the game balences the magic weapons, too. the shotgun, for instense, is very powerful and can one-shot a lot of enemies. to prevent you from just using it over and over again, the game makes its more powerful weapons use mp, and the main way to recover mp is by hitting enemies with melee weapons. the game isn't without flaws, tho. i personally don't mind it, but there is a durability system in the game and i know that is something that may turn people away. weapons can recover fairly quickly by holstering them at your side or back, and the game will let you know if a weapon's durability is low by making it glow red so there's no fear of loosing your really good weapons. if anything, it just encourages you to switch up your playstyle every now and then, which isn't a problem since there are so many fun weapons. but if you have your heart set on using one specific weapon, that it stuns them, only that you can block attacks. and unlike the red eye attacks, enemies who are parried with normal attacks will just stand there, which makes it feel like there is a problem with surv1v3 is an interesting and enjoyable game. at time of writing i have almost 40 hours in it and there will likely be another 40 before i put it away but, despite the positive review i'm giving it, i do want to temper expectations. unfortunately, this is another vr game recommendation because vr is young and the number of enjoyable games is limited. if this was a standard game, it wouldn’t be getting a thumbs up in its current state.

that being said, it was/is still a good bit of fun and, if you like co-op games, this is the best i've run across so far!

the good:
- the game is a blast to play with friends. 2 people is great, 3 people gives you a lot of flexibility and 4 player is an optional, though currently experimental, setting.
- the atmosphere is quite nice. sometimes spooky, sometimes open, sometimes claustrophobic.
- gunplay is enjoyable once you get used to it.
- story is fun and the devs got a lot of good use out of the couple maps the game currently has.
- progression/advancement is interesting through the use of pickupable instructional books.
- fair bit of variety throughout the game.
- co-op gameplay is really satisfying.
- a functional, mostly ui-free game that pulls the style off quite well.

the bad:
- if you aren’t a gun person, the game mechanics can feel esoteric. the game doesn't give you a whole lot of information on its systems so you just kinda have to go with some trial and error (or ask your gun friend).
- melee physics aren’t great. technically functional but very hit or miss.
- you have to watch the candymaker and unreal logo every time you go back to the main menu and, since you can't change a lot of the options while in game, you'll probably end up returning to the main menu quite a bit (one time on game startup is quite enough please!).
- suboptimal network performance in multiplayer; often have teammates that will crash to the main menu at seemingly random points.
- random gameplay bugs like the broken hand bug, sticky item bug, floating ammunition bug, etc. not game breaking but consistently around to break immersion
- throwing items is awful. you simply can't throw a bomb or explosive canister with the current system.
- enemy type is limited to 5 varieties with some having a couple slight alterations for variation that are all defeated in the same way (bullet to the face). there are a couple 'boss' zombies too but they account for less than 1% of the total gameplay.
- physics can get really weird; stretched limbs and zombie heads poking through walls or closed doors.

the other:
- game is not balanced for when you add more players; additional people just makes the game categorically easier.
- difficulty options change very little of the game. wish there was more options for tweaking the gameplay.
- using a laser sight eliminates a lot of the gunplay and challenge.
- some of the progression through the book pickups dont make sense such as being able to use a gun if it's already loaded with explosive ammo even if you haven't picked up its associated book but, if you eject the mag to check your ammo count, you can't put the mag back in the gun(?).
- far too many resources with no time pressure. i found it fairly common to be loaded to the teeth with two pistols and a full belt of explosive rounds, two (or sometimes three) primary weapons, a pair of melee weapons and enough health kits to go for days. the lack of any time pressure means you can spend as much time as you like scavenging for resources to make sure the game is a walk in the park.
- weaponry doesn't carry over between levels in story mode so you end up starting from scratch on each level. oddly, your loadout is saved on survival mode.
- story level's length is super variable, could be anything from 20 minutes to 2 hours and it's hard to know what you're signing up for.
- if any teammate dies before you open a safe house, the story mission restarts. just weird that your starting room isn’t considered a 'safe house' for this purpose.
- player ik is a bit wonky. you would think humanoid ik would be a solve problem in this day and age but surv1v3's kinematics aren't great and causes a lot of bent and broken arms and flailing body parts at times. not really a problem for me but it was worth noting in a review as it is a bit immersion breaking to have gumby arms one minute and pretzel limbs the next.


i do very much hope the developers continue making content. i would totally buy another dlc campaign and i hope to see improvements for the existing systems. the current survival mode is neat but lacks an engaging drive to play since it's really just bouncing between a couple houses to collect respawning resources while endlessly shooting zombies. the random missions are a nice carrot but they just give you more of the same resources you could already find in the world. would be fun to have noted boss targets, wave spawns, resource collections, escort quests, etc, littered throughout the map for players to work toward and gain additional rewards for.

in the end, the game is very worth the $25 in my opinion and, if candymakers continues improving from here, it will only get better :)

i'll keep this brief. while it's neat to have a real mmo in vr, something i've been waiting for since the original .hack//sign, they made all the worst decisions in terms of the game itself.

sure it's ugly but that's to be expected at this point and can be forgiven. what can't be forgiven are the game mechanics. instead of focusing on making a fun mmo for vr they focused on recreating the same experience of the once popular cookie-cutter mmo's of the past. boring fetch quests, areas of mindless mobs you grind, completely boring slow combat, etc. the problem is all it's parts are completely generic and worse than any mmo you've played before, it's only saving trait is vr. admittedly some of the things are cool in vr, like the potion and lure crafting, but i find this is the exception. 

you'll see the one common praise for this game is the social aspect. there are other games with a better social aspect for free without the dated mmo mechanics bogging it down. this game didn't offer any unique social interactions other than being forced to talk to other players if you wanted to learn more. npc's will actually say this instead of giving you more information.

while some of the game is cool ultimately all the negatives far out way the positives. with the large price tag it's even more reason to avoid this title unless you were an mmoholic 10 years ago. this is the quality i'd expect from the first f2p vr mmo not the first premium game. if you removed vr no one would want to play it because it's simply a subpar and generic mmo and adding vr doesn't add enough to the appeal to make it worth playing. it's not that i hate it or it's the worst game ever i'm just very disappointed by it being so bland and unappealing when it's a genre i'm perhaps the most excited for.

sorry i didn't end up keeping it brief, i suppose my disappointment is greater than i thought. i at least have to give them props for doing a free weekend so i didn't have to refund it.

rags to dishes is a very good vr game of fast paced food preparation.
the challenges are nicely put together, the stress factor is present and the customers are impatient.

in the game you are a new owner of a very classic snack bar from the medieval era.
you will therefore be on the marketplace with your store and prepare customer orders in time.
cheese bread, fried fish or sausage, oatmeal, soup, and much more.
please note, you cannot prepare a supply of food to sell it pre-prepared, it is required to give the dishes as fresh as possible to the customers, so rushing it quickly is certainly good once the customers gave their orders, still you'll have your hands full when you wait for customers.

the game also rewards the player with extensions for your snack bar that allow you to make more dishes, make them faster, and even employees.
you can choose these rewards by exchanging scored points with your choices in the in-game shop.

the environment is also very nice in the game, a bit cartoonish but a nice medieval environment.

it is also important to know that you must set your room setting for steamvr accurately, the game uses approximately the entire area unless you have a very very large room.

when i look at this game analytically, i usually end up landing on about a 6/10 for this game. the story feels practically non-existent and i didn't really have any idea what was going on. i've looked at discussions about the story and people are talking characters and companies that i never knew about in the game. i understand that some people like stories where you really have to dig into the world to uncover the bigger picture and piece things together but the fact that i can play this game from start to finish and have absolutely no idea what the story even was is poor storytelling.

the melee combat is kind of fun but sharp objects particularly don't feel impactful. the enemies feel like they're made of butter and all my weapons just slide into them with zero effort (you can just stand still, hold out a sword in front of you and watch the enemy walk into it and impale themselves with no effort on your part). there's an argument to be made that this is done with the purpose of making the combat less finicky but after playing saints & sinners where both the sound design and force required to use sharp weapons makes them feel much more satisfying to use, going back to boneworks really makes you notice how weak they can feel.

the movement can be janky at times, parts of your simulated body will just get caught on things in the environment causing you to get stuck for a moment. or maybe your arms will phase through a wall, meaning you're just stood there trying to yank your virtual arms free until the game eventually grants your wish. i appreciate the effort that went into creating this simulated body and it feels great at times, but can also feel like more of a detriment at others.

gunplay is where this game truly shines. guns feel satisfying to shoot and reload and when combined with slow motion, this game becomes the prime vr candidate for living out your john wick fantasies. you have three types of pistols (each with a different balance of magazine size to damage per bullet), an smg and an assault rifle with different variants for things like holosights and laser sights. sadly there are no shotguns which is a shame since they seem perfect for sending enemies flying with this game's advanced vr physics, so hopefully we could get that in a later patch.

but despite all that, i really think this game is greater than the sum of its parts. despite the fact that i believe both half-life: alyx and saints & sinners are better vr experiences and just better games, i always find myself coming back to boneworks when i want my fix of fun vr combat. and although i do think this game suffers from a bit of innovation imperative, valuing new and interesting ideas above all else even when they don't work as well in practice as they sound on paper, i will absolutely respect this game for trying to push vr gaming forward as a medium because even when these kinds of games make missteps they are important for pushing the platform forward and encouraging other developers to experiment as well.

the slopes is a ski-based runner, placing players on a finite trail filled with obstacles and coins. the trail itself is stagnant, and it remains the same for every run; there is no procedural generation here. the ultimate goal is to get from the starting point to the finish line while dodging trees, rocks, boulders, and bushes while collecting as many coins as possible.

despite the plethora of obstacles along the trail, there is no penalty for hitting any of them. if you really wanted to, you could just take a straight path and keep rowing your ski poles to regain speed. the only factor that even matters in the slightest are the coins, which make up the entire portion of your score. sadly there are no leaderboards, so it's just you trying to outdo your best coin collecting. overall time from point a to point b is not even taken in to account.

at the end of it all, the slopes is an extremely basic mini-game that comes with no distinct challenges; only the ones that you'll mentally set for yourself, if you so choose to do so. there aren't even any jumps, and although the store page says it's a "downhill race", the entire map is one long stretch of level snow. the run takes about three minutes to complete, even while hitting a variety of the obstructions, and beyond that there is very little replayability. the idea is a good one, but the execution is terrible, and for it to be close to being worth the small $2.19 cad pricetag, some new features would need to be implemented.

the game takes a long time to boot up, to the point where it will make you think it crashed. if you get passed that, the headset may not display the game. to fix that, you gotta aim your headset towards the clipboard and go to the options menu to disable bloom. 

thats the tech issues out of the way, but this vr game is very much of the past. playing it reminded me of the first oculus rift dev kit. motion sickness hit me like a truck within the first 15 min. the borders did not match the play area either, so i had to walk forward and reset the position for me to reach all my tools. the hands kinda did whatever they wanted and freaked out when i was about to make a cut during the brain operation, killing bob. 

this game needs polish. it is such a shame that it seem to be abandoned, as im kinda fond of the game. this is not a game you should have to pay for in its current state!

i love it. stride has a certain flow to it which just nails it for me. i feel like i’m fast and i’m flying because of my own movements, which is fantastic and exactly what i was looking for. it has that “just one more try” feeling for me where i essentially just keep trying again and never actually quit. no other game has made me completely fight through muscle pain because it was so fun. beat saber is not even close. but there’s just not much there yet. what you see in the first 2 trailers is all there is right now. the main reason i’ve been playing for so long is just for that awesome flow feeling, but also because i was gunning for the number 1 spot on the leaderboard. which i got hold of temporarily! anyway, the game has great mechanics and a nice concept but very little game to back it up, for now. what there is also needs some polish. 

currently there’s only an endless mode in which you run through 3 sections (easy, medium, hard) which all have about 10-15 sub sections (max. i’m being generous) which the game strings together randomly. after you survive for some time the levels of the next difficulty tier start appearing and the enemies shoot you way faster. which leads me to the hard levels.
the hard levels are unpolished and unfair. in order to beat them you have to know exactly where the enemies spawn, when they spawn and what the route you need to take looks like. in some cases you can barely outrun the zone even if you cut perfect diagonal lines and know exactly what’s coming. the snipers materialize, aim, and kill you within what feels like 0,5 seconds. compared to the easy 2 seconds of the first level. you’ll be walking and suddenly you’ll be dead. unless you know where they spawn, where the invisible trigger that spawns them is and anticipate by slowing down time. 

the controls i find to be overall good and consistent, but very specific in unobvious and unexplained ways. for example: to wallrun you need to jump and look into the wall slightly while holding your movement stick forward. this is not obvious since you can run by just shaking your hands, without holding the movement stick. jump into a wall like that and you’ll just fall down. i died a lot of times because i didn’t know this specific mechanical requirement, it always felt frustrating and unfair. once i learned how it worked however it has been very consistent. 

i’m absolutely loving my time playing what there currently is, and i cannot understate how much i enjoy the core gameplay loop, but there isn’t a whole lot there yet. the game has a lot of potential but, as is common with early access games, for the current price tag ‘potential’ is also a large part of what you’ll be spending your money on.

this app is life-changing. i didn't look at any reviews upon purchase and i'm happy i didn't. covid's aftermath left me disjoined and stressed about further career moves. i've always been a big supporter of exercise, yoga, and meditation, but i found i needed to be somewhat physically exerted to obtain calmness with meditation. i bought this app on a whim about 10 months ago, and i (and the people around me) have noticed a considerable difference. 

1) the "game" some are referring to is the "focus" meditation, which i use before every study session, and it has improved my grades remarkably. it's only 8 minutes long, which is perfect for when you have a lot of work to do, and not a lot of time to do it. if you have attention deficit problems, this is worth a try.

2) the "normal" meditation is under the "calm," which has much longer sessions. yes, there have been times, especially in the beginning when i was still learning, that i've run through two sessions on calm to get the desired effect. however, i've been using this app regularly and have found it takes me far less time to feel the effects. 

3) some comments said the rating at the beginning and end ruins the meditation. i like rating how i feel at the beginning and end. especially while i was learning, it helped me figure what worked and what didn't work for me (e.g., postures, breathing techniques outside the guided ones, which guided breathing techniques worked best for me, etc.). additionally, it's very easy to forget how crappy you felt when you started; it's kind of the entire point of meditation, actually. so having that reminder at the end kept me coming back, helping me form the long-term mindful practices i have today. 

this is a steal for what it cost. i 100% recommend this to everyone i know. 

to the creators of this app, you are doing amazing work and helping people in a very real way. you should be very proud, i'm proud of you.

this game is the best battle royale experience that you can have in vr right now. im playing on the quest 2 and im always blown away by what this little headset can do without a pc. the map is huge, the game runs smoothly, and the gameplay is fun and fast paced. i do wish that games would last a little longer but maybe in the future we will get more than 18 players. i would describe this game as slightly arcady in a way but its not a bad thing, it just means that things get simplified where they can be, to make gameplay smoother. i do wish that i could get rid of the floating crosshair but i dont hate it and in fact it comes in handy now and then. another thing that really separates this game is the vertical aspect. you can climb anything and you can glide long distances. it brings a whole different element to the game. especially because you can also build quick cover. if you really get into it you can climb very fast and get a good shoulder workout at the same time lol. the sniper is a little wonky because when you ads it goes full screen sniper scope view, but i was practicing with it against bots (did i mention you can practice against bots? very good feature) and if you get used to it, its not terrible. overall i am extremely satisfied with my purchase and i paid full price, i was also not part of any early beta testing. i was skeptical when i saw another battle royale for vr because so many of them sucked, but this game really delivered for me. also its crossbuy so thats something i appreciate from a dev. 4 thumbs up. 11/10 also one last thing, the community so far has been some of the best ive experienced in vr shooters.

this is a fantastic, polished sword fighting roguelike. normally i hate roguelikes, but with vr it works out ok as i never want to play for long stretches of time anyway. from the makers of i expect you to die, this shows just as much care and attention to both gameplay mechanics and the opportunities of vr. it's definitely a challenging game though, you need very quick reactions and the enemies get difficult very quickly. the animations are pretty good, the sound and music are awesome, and the game does a really good job of making you feel like a sword master.

my only real criticisms so far are:
- the indicators for where to place your swords to block an attack do not stand out enough visually, so sometimes i get killed by an attack i didn't even know was coming.
- if you want to progress, you basically have to just choose "money" as the reward at the end of every arena rather than improving your gear, because you get a tiny amount of cash to spend on upgrades if you don't. i'd like to see more cash as a reward for completing a level so you don't have to just grind the same first few levels lots of times to improve your weapons
- i wouldn't mind a slightly longer difficulty curve. the stages seem to be the same every time rather than random, and while i am continually making progress, i find it consistently very difficult to dodge in time; you get about 400 milliseconds of an arrow telling you which way to throw yourself before you get killed

nevertheless, vr bring the immersion to the maximum, being able to be in this world in vr is awesome, it's the first vr game to bring that to the table.

great entry point to military flight sims; the aircraft systems/cockpits are realistic enough to be satisfying to learn and use, without delving into the byzantine complexities of the true sims out there. that's not to say this game isn't complex; you can still expect some wiki reading to get the most out of the various weapons systems.

the virtual flight controls take some getting used to (especially if you are used to holding a physical flight stick), but after a few hours it feels fairly natural. honestly though, for a beginner, this game is great for that reason; no need to buy a hotas setup, so it's a good way to see if you enjoy milsim flight games before making an investment in a good setup. 

overall 9/10, my only complaint is the relative lack of aircraft, but seeing as how this is a solo dev project, it's completely understandable. the aircraft that are in the game are very well polished, with distinct "feels" for each. 

side note: this game has an incredible terrain and mission editor, almost as good as the arma series (and in some ways better). if you're like me, that is a huge selling point alone; at this point i probably have more hours in the editor than in the cockpit.

the tutorial shows you the simple to use controls and how to "blink" (teleporting allowing you to move further , but still only within your line of sight) in a good way allowing  for a smooth ride that makes it fun to explore and expirence the wonderful world around you.

the world is pretty detailed and allows interaction with enough things to make it fun to just stay and play around for a while at certain spots.

the story is interesting and it unfolds in a good way, giving enough hints to let you move along at a good pace but still leaves some things to figure out by yourself. to a pretty large degree it's puzzel solving that takes you to the next step, and in there was no fighting at all in this episode, but it was not needed to get you you excited and build up a tense feeling.

this was simply a great first episode of a game that i hope will continue to provide as great episodes, but that hopefully are a bit longer (i played this episode from start to end in less than an hour). it really made me want to buy the next episode, not only to contue to explore, but also to see how the story unfolds (it hints of a quite different direction, but that might not be a bad thing if the game play and environment is of the same quality as in this first episode).

i do strongly recommend it.
